children: The company introduces a suite of AI products to close the conversation gap across Zoom Workplace, customer experience, developer tools, and events
-- Today at its annual Zoomtopia customer conference, Zoom Communications, Inc.

, a leading AI-first platform for human connection, introduced a new Unified Context Layer and several new products with AI-powered capabilities. The new offerings are designed to help businesses transform rich meeting context into meaningful deliverables that help accelerate work outcomes.

Business conversations drive critical decisions and build customer history every day. A customer interaction might start in a meeting, continue by phone, and carry on in chat threads. But when that context is scattered across applications, people and AI agents lose the thread and teams spend significant time piecing together what happened, when it happened, and what they should do about it.
helps close that gap by linking conversation history with relevant documents and data. Together, these sources give people and AI agents a fuller picture of the work and what needs to happen next.

This new layer brings together conversations with near real-time activity across Zoom and connected third-party applications, giving people and AI agents access to business context that might otherwise be lost or siloed. Configurable settings and controls help manage access, while coordination among AI agents turns business context into actionable insights.
Zoom is increasingly becoming a system of action as organizations, large and small, put the company's AI tools to work at scale.

Zoom Virtual Agent customer count has surged by 256%1, and users who leverage Zoom's various AI tools report completing tasks twice as fast, with 72% citing high or extremely high business impact, compared with a market average of 63%2. Zoom is expecting to surpass $5 billion in annual revenue this year.

With a growing enterprise footprint across industries from healthcare to financial services, retail, and education, the company is advancing its vision for workplace productivity, one where the line between conversation and execution shrinks.
“AI models are only as powerful as their understanding of your business, and that context makes all the difference,” said
Eric Yuan, founder and CEO of Zoom

. “Fragmented product experiences isolate conversations, stall decisions, and drag businesses down. Today, with the Unified Context Layer, we’re laying the groundwork for a system of action designed to turn conversations into completed work.”
“Our teams have the information they need, but it’s often dispersed across meetings, notes, and different systems,” said
Christine Sarros, senior vice president of Enterprise Engineering, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure

. “Zoom’s new solutions could help bring that context together, so teams can enter customer conversations with a clearer understanding of what’s been discussed, what’s been decided, and what needs to happen next. We see an opportunity to spend less time reconstructing history and more time helping our customers move forward.”

At Zoomtopia, Zoom is bringing this vision to life with innovations across collaboration, AI, customer experience, and events. The announcements below show how it all connects business context to the tools and workflows people actually use to get work done.
Give people and AI agents context to turn conversations into action
Every meeting, chat, and document leaves a trail of discussion, decisions, and action items. Zoom's
accesses this information to help people and AI agents quickly move from context to clarity to action.
The Unified Context Layer makes work even more efficient when used with the newly introduced capabilities that include:
Delivers personalized transcripts and summaries for users who miss all or parts of a meeting.
Links shared screens, slides, charts, and in-meeting chat to relevant moments in a searchable transcript.
Extends My Notes to in-person conversations through new devices from DTEN and Bota.

Turn meeting summaries into follow-up work in everyday tools like Zoom Chat and Salesforce, with ready-made workflows for sales, marketing, and IT, or custom ones created by describing what to automate in natural language, no separate workflow builder needed to get started.
A refreshed chat experience designed to help surface relevant conversations and bring AI agents directly into discussions to take actions based on administrator-defined controls.
Specialized AI agents that work together in an AI team to support faster execution of work.
Bring Zoom capabilities into the AI tools businesses already use

can now access Zoom capabilities outside the Zoom app. Through APIs and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, teams can connect scheduling, transcription, search, administration, and contact center actions to other AI environments and workflows. Highlights include:
With new MCP servers across the portfolio, developers and AI agents can coordinate actions outside the Zoom UI.
Use supported Zoom capabilities within AI environments, including Claude, Codex, Copilot, and Muse.
Query Zoom's Unified Context Layer directly from Claude, GPT, Codex, Muse, MS Copilot, Gemini, and Slackbot, as well as MCP-compatible agents.
Reduce barriers to natural, engaging conversation
To help users show up as their best in

, Zoom is making conversations clearer, more natural, and more inclusive, with AI driving more meaningful outcomes. These new enhancements strengthen the foundation for the unified context layer with:
"Translate Me" enables a speaker to translate their audio for all participants using a synthesized version of their own voice, designed to preserve a natural feel.
Subtly adjusts a user’s video when they glance away from the camera, helping maintain a camera-forward appearance.
Users can use this feature to alter their own voice with real-time accent smoothing so speakers come through more clearly and naturally.
Enhanced media support for 60 frames per second screen sharing.
Proactive meeting assistance that helps find answers, keep meetings on track, and nudge engagement.
Carry customer history from one interaction to the next
Customer service breaks down when customers have to constantly repeat themselves, and agents have to reconstruct past interactions
extends shared customer context across a variety of channels, including live and AI agents, providing a broader view of the past and present to help inform future outcomes. Highlights include:
Brings dynamic customer profiles into Zoom CX with real-time context across channels and interactions.
Automatically classifies voice, chat, and email transcripts and makes them queryable in natural language, joined with operational data, such as handle time, queue, and outcome.
Brings AI-powered self-service to physical retail locations via branded kiosk agents, resolving customer requests on the spot without relying onin-store staff.

that enable administrators to manage AI activity across the account while supporting customers' existing guardrails and data-classification policies. Highlights include:
Provides administrators with greater control over how AI features are configured and used across the organization.
Seamlessly sync with Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels or create native labels in Zoom, then automatically enforce policies based on the sensitivity of meetings and content.

Zoom Compliance Manager support for My Notes and Zoom Canvas:
Archives and monitors AI-generated summaries, notes, and documents to help address organization's own retention and supervision requirements3.
Extend the business value of events beyond the closing session

Most of what happens at a live event disappears the moment it ends. Zoom Events now brings powerful AI functionality to event planning, content creation, and analytics. These capabilities help reduce the amount of heavy setup work involved and extend the value of event content long after sessions end. Highlights include:
Turn one recording into a multi-language, multi-format asset library.
Use AI to help configure event details, from sessions to registration, before launch.
Query event data in plain language, score engagement, and generate shareable reports, cutting post-event analysis time significantly.
